evals.prompt: Case A. send file.pdf to a@example.com, no cc, subject or message, default expiry is fine
evals.expected_output: All optional fields settled, so no question: a dry run, then a Share card with the default expiry, CC/Subject/Message shown as None, and a wait for Y/yes. Nothing is sent.
expectations: Runs `send ... --dry-run --json` and never runs `send` without `--dry-run`
Shows the Share card with `To` = a@example.com
The card shows `CC`, `Subject` and `Message` each as `None`
The card shows `Expires in` with the dry run's `access_expiration` and `(default)`
Right below the card's code block, outside it, the reply says `Type Y or yes to confirm.` and `N to cancel, or tell me what to change.`, and nothing follows it
The card shows a `Team` block first (`Your personal team` when personal, or the team name alone)
The card is inside a text code block and contains no `**` or backticks

evals.prompt: Case B. send file.pdf to a@example.com expired 10 days  (the plan allows at most 4 days)
evals.expected_output: The short three-line expiry error suggesting 4 days. Nothing uploaded or sent, draft kept.
expectations: Output starts with `❌ Expiration is too long.`
States the 4-day maximum and ends with a reply the user can type, such as `Reply **4** to use 4 days`
Shows no error code, exit code, status, raw JSON or plan/quota explanation
Offers one suggestion, not a list of options
Never runs `send` without `--dry-run`
The error is plain chat text, not inside a code block, so `**4 days**` renders as bold

evals.prompt: Case B, second turn. Earlier: user asked to send file.pdf to a@example.com expiring in 10 days, and you replied with the 'Expiration is too long' error (max 4 days). User now says: 4 days (user said: no cc, no subject, no message, default expiry)
evals.expected_output: Expiry updated to 4 days, dry run re-run, new Share card; recipient and file are not asked again.
expectations: Does not ask again for recipients or files
Re-runs the dry run with `--expires-in 4d`
Shows the Share card with `Expires in` = 4 days, without `(default)`
